phases.label: Weeks 1–4
phases.subtitle: Start here
phases.note: Differin only 2× this phase. Wide spacing (Mon → Thu) gives skin time to adapt. Mild tightness is normal. Flaking around nose/mouth in week 3–4 — cover with balm, don't pick. Move on when skin has been calm for a full week.

phases.label: Weeks 5–8
phases.subtitle: Then this
phases.note: Differin now 3×, glycolic paused. Skin may briefly look worse in weeks 5–6 (purging) — do not stop. By week 7–8 texture smooths. Move on when calm for a full week.

phases.label: Week 9+

phases.note: The permanent schedule. Full rotation with all products. Stay here. Pea-size Differin, cotton pad for acids, eye area always spared.

safetyRules.title: Never combine adapalene and acids
safetyRules.rule: Adapalene together with AHA or BHA in one application massively irritates the skin without boosting results. Always separate nights. To exfoliate the same day: BHA in the morning, adapalene at night — and only when skin is calm.

safetyRules.title: Retinoid without SPF is net-negative
safetyRules.rule: Retinoids temporarily increase UV sensitivity. Without daily sunscreen, new pigmentation forms faster than the retinoid clears old damage. If you are not committed to SPF every day, do not start adapalene.

safetyRules.title: Two finger-lengths of SPF, or it is useless
safetyRules.rule: SPF ratings are tested at 2 mg/cm² — roughly two strips along the index and middle finger for face and neck. Most people apply a quarter of that and get an effective SPF of ~15.

safetyRules.title: Never rub the eye area — always tap
safetyRules.rule: Under-eye skin is 4× thinner than the rest of the face. Repeated rubbing causes chronic micro-inflammation, which drives the very pigmentation you are treating. Ring finger only — it applies the least pressure by reflex.

safetyRules.title: Judge at week 12, not week 3
safetyRules.rule: Vitamin C, adapalene and niacinamide need 8–12 weeks to show visible change. Photos every 4 weeks in the same lighting beat the daily mirror check.

safetyRules.title: High Focus Shot (MFU) boundaries
safetyRules.rule: Maximum once per week. Completely avoid the eyeballs, eyelids, jawbone edge, lips and the centre of the neck (thyroid area). Target only the jowls, lower face sag and the sides of the neck.

safetyRules.title: The no-mix actives rule
safetyRules.rule: Never use the Exosome Shot or the Booster Pro Air Shot on the same night as 0.2% Retinol, and never on a High Focus Shot night.

safetyRules.title: The conductivity rule
safetyRules.rule: Use a thick layer of PDRN Booster Gel for the High Focus Shot, or PDRN Pink Peptide Serum for the Booster Pro. Oils (Freiöl, Rose Hip Oil) insulate — always apply them after device use, never before.

safetyRules.title: The 'Kalk' hard-water shield
safetyRules.rule: Hamburg tap water dulls skin and stretches pores. Use the Foreo in the evening to strip mineral buildup mechanically, and always apply The Ordinary HA 2% + B5 while the skin is still damp.

hair._status: SHARED — one protocol, both people. Amounts and two treatments differ per person.

context.why: Sulfates strip natural oils from dense Asian hair, so the cuticle stays open and the texture turns rough and stiff. Conditioning seals it. On top of that, hard water leaves a calcium/magnesium film on every strand — that is what the weekly rinse removes.
context.verify: Test your own shower tap with strips on day 1 and again at week 8. The district average is a guess; your tap is the real number.

everyShower._note: Four steps, every wash, both of you. The citric rinse is NOT part of this — it is weekly.

steps.how: Warm water. Work in from the roots, massage the scalp for ~60 sec. Check the INCI label — no SLS or SLES.
Warm water. A cold 10-second finish is fine if you like it, but the cold itself does not seal the cuticle — the weekly citric rinse does that.
Microfiber only. Press and squeeze sections. Rubbing roughens the cuticle and causes frizz.
Apply to damp hair. Do not rinse out.

perPerson.philipp: Pea-sized amount. Start at the ends and work up slightly — short hair needs less.
perPerson.eunice: 2–3× more product. Work from the ends up through the full length before touching the roots.

scheduled.title: Citric acid rinse
scheduled.recipe: ¼ tsp citric acid per 500 ml warm water — target pH 4–5. Not ½ tsp; that is too acidic.
scheduled.order: Shampoo → rinse → pour the citric solution over all hair → wait 1–2 min → rinse out → leave-in as normal.
scheduled.why: At 17.3 °dH weekly is the right frequency. The acid dissolves the calcium/magnesium film that makes hair feel coated and stiff.
scheduled.caution: Straw-like texture, brittleness, more tangles or scalp itch mean you are overdoing it. Do not go to 2× weekly, and stay at ¼ tsp.

scheduled.title: Chelating shampoo
scheduled.recipe: Malibu C Hard Water Wellness — use in place of your regular shampoo.
scheduled.order: Lather, leave on 3–5 min, rinse fully. Follow immediately with a deep conditioner or your leave-in — do not skip that.
scheduled.why: EDTA binds calcium and magnesium ions inside the hair shaft and pulls them out when you rinse. Regular shampoo — even sulfate-free — physically cannot do this.
scheduled.caution: Strips moisture and protein if used too often. Every 2–3 weeks is enough; the weekly citric rinse handles maintenance in between.

scheduled.title: Deep conditioning mask
scheduled.recipe: Any mask with glycerin, panthenol or argan oil — Cantu, OGX or Garnier.
scheduled.order: After shampooing, before the citric rinse. Leave on 5–10 min in the shower steam, then rinse, run the citric rinse, apply leave-in.
scheduled.why: Longer hair needs deeper conditioning to prevent split ends and manage tangling. Philipp's length does not need this layer.

shampoo._note: Priority order — grab whichever you find first.

options.name: Cantu Sulfate-Free Cleansing Cream
options.note: Built for dense, coarse hair — the right match for both of you. Good lather despite being sulfate-free. Strong enough for 17.3 °dH.

options.name: HASK Repair + Argan Oil
options.note: 473 ml, no SLS/SLES. Uses Sodium C14-16 Olefin Sulfonate — stronger than ideal, but better than classic sulfates.

options.name: Alverde Ultra Sensitiv
options.note: Cleanest INCI of all, but likely too gentle for dense hair at this hardness. Higher risk for Eunice — more mineral surface area. Switch back to Cantu if the scalp feels unclean after 48h.

leaveIn._note: A leave-in you don't rinse out — its job is to re-soften the cuticle the hard water roughened. A rich cream suits long, dense hair; a light keratin or oil spray suits short hair. Either works — the one thing to avoid is using a rinse-out conditioner as a leave-in. For a cream, look for glycerin or panthenol high on the INCI.

options.name: Garnier Fructis Leave-in Creme Aloe Air Dry
options.note: This is the current name for the old "Hair Drink" — Garnier renamed the line, which is why searching the old name found nothing. Glycerin sits high on its list, exactly the humectant this protocol wants. Grab it in the aisle; Amazon stock is patchy.

options.name: Cantu Shea Butter Leave-In Repair Cream
options.note: Same brand as your shampoo, built for dense, coarse hair. Search Amazon.de for "Cantu Leave-In" — reliably stocked there. Richer than the Garnier: pea-size for Philipp, 2–3× for Eunice.

options.name: Garnier Fructis Schadenlöscher 10-in-1 Leave-in (spray)
options.rank: A spray — good for short hair
options.note: A keratin-and-oil spray rather than a glycerin cream — a different tool for the same job, and the lighter one. Ideal for short hair (Philipp): a spritz or two on damp ends, off the scalp; it also protects to 230 °C if you heat-style. Fine on long hair too (Eunice) — if it ever feels stiff or straw-like over weeks, that is keratin build-up, so drop to every other wash.

options.name: Any leave-in with glycerin or panthenol near the top
options.note: The brand does not matter. A cream or milk with glycerin/panthenol high, ideally a light oil (argan/shea) too. Skip anything led by silicones (an ingredient ending -cone or -xane first) — at 17.3 °dH they build up.

towel.name: Microfiber hair towel
towel.note: Any brand. Get two, one each.

citricAcid.name: Heitmann Citronensäure Pulver
citricAcid.note: Food-grade. One pack lasts months. Optional: pH strips (~€3–5) to confirm pH 4–5.

chelator.name: Malibu C Hard Water Wellness
chelator.inci: Disodium or Tetrasodium EDTA high on the list. EDTA near the bottom is only a preservative and will not chelate.

rollout.goldenRule: Change one thing at a time. Starting shampoo, leave-in and the citric rinse together means you will never know what worked. Stagger each change by about a week.

Only after 8–12 weeks of package A with no improvement.
Only if stiffness clearly persists despite regular chelating.
Confirm tap hardness with strips first.
packages.note: Most people at 17 °dH get enough relief from the chemical approach alone.

How long to fully comb wet hair without snagging. Log a benchmark before week 1. Track per person.
Hair in the drain catch per session. Very variable day to day — read the trend over 4+ sessions.
Test the shower tap on day 1, retest at week 8.

hair._cadenceNote: everyDays is the numeric form of the cadence text, so the page can answer 'is it due today?' instead of leaving the date arithmetic to the reader. everyDaysMax, where present, is the far end of a range cadence — past it the treatment reads as late rather than merely due.
hair._sequenceNote: replacesStep / afterStep / rank say where a treatment lands in the everyShower list, so the page can build one numbered sequence for today. The prose in each `order` field still explains the treatment on its own; this is what lets three of them be read as a single shower. Chelating REPLACES the shampoo rather than following it. The mask goes before the citric rinse, which is what the mask's own order sentence already said.
